svg.title: inequalities preceding (WS3) permit these shifts so the inspected insertion cells are disjoint. Apply Cauchy–Schwarz in the positive reflection form successively in the separating coordinate directions. Each insertion contributes its centered seminorm at most Ak; no factor depends on the volume or the microscopic cutoff. Thus the finite Wilson word has magnitude at most An k. Take its ordered mesh and period limits at a coordinate-generic tuple. The fitted coefficients converge in their finite-dimensional balls, and multilinearity permits them to vary along the limit. The same bound passes to the limiting correlation. On the open set of tuples with some separating coordinate for each pair, the correlation is continuous and the generic tuples have full measure and are dense. Therefore the bound extends to every tuple in that open set. This proves the first part of (WS3) on the entire separated window, including coordinate ties.
